newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money closes down, security prices up.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money closes down, security prices up.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed lower at 2.25-3.00 percent on Tuesday, off day's opening levels of 3.75-4.25 percent, dealers said.
Most of the deals were in the band of 3.25-3.75 percent, they said.
The rates will open at 3.0 percent on Wednesday and will fall to 1.5-2.0 percent towards the close, a dealer said.
The interbank term money market showed some activity on Tuesday, a dealer said. Three month money was dealt in the region of 9.75-10.25 percent, he said
The redeemption of 12.00 percent government stock 1997 on June 5, will add 10.0 billion rupees into the system, dealers said.
The easy money conditions clubbed with redemptions and interest payments on government stock will ease the call rates to a greater extent, they said.
The security market sentiment improved on easy call levels. Prices of securtities rose by 10-15 basis points for short to medium term papers, dealers said.
The volume on National Stock Exchange (NSE) rose to 5.0 billion rupees on Tuesday, against the previous 4.3 billion rupees, a NSE dealer said.

He said most of the activity was centred in the newly auctioned paper, 12.14 percent 2000, which was dealt in the range of 100.10 rupees to 100.30 rupees, at a volume of 2.0 billion rupees, against its previous price of 100.12 rupees.

The 13.50 percent stock rose to 101.10 rupees, against its previous close of 100.99 rupees, 13.50 percent 1998 rose to 102.95 from 102.75, 13.85 percent 2001 rose to 104.55 from 104.30, while the 12.69 percent 2002 traded in the range of 100.65 to 100.76 rupees, compared to previous 100.60 rupees.
